To address bogman's comment about questioning a cultivar, I think that's a completely valid point, but it's more of a case by case situation. for example, S. Ellie Wang is unquestionable, nothing out there like it, and the colors are ridiculous, it's easy to grow, easy to color up, pretty much bling-bling by all means. But I've bred plants in the past that I didn't personally deem worthy and they were almost trashed, yet it turns out growers find it very popular! Case and point, S. Leuco burgundy x minor giant 'pink clone' is : sarracenia.proboards.com/thread/438/leuco-burgundy-minor-giant-clone

Bogman: do you think that black Sarracenia I bred (the one that colors up relatively easily) has crappy shape? I heard such feedback and come to think of it, I agree, seems like the shape can be improved. What do you think? If another black plant with better shape is bred, maybe that black one isn't all that and won't stand the test of time.
Well meizzwang, in the end, it's up to you to decide. Case by case is true, to be sure. Registering is a bit of "paperwork" and you'll need to address the many look-alikes; should they be included if the traits are very similar? If not, what makes it unique?

"The best" is, at most, a temporary opinion. The registration process really is more important as a way to standardize a name for a cultivar which is apt to be, or has been, distributed. For example, if meizzwang sends me one a those black things, it could be a code letter/number or cultivar name, like "Bogman's Torment", LOL!

Crappy shape? Has this dark baby reached mature size? I have no problem with the shape, but it's really hard to tell from pictures. You know, it's easier to tell in real life. And... it might grow to a different shape in Virginia. heh heh. It looks like a landmark in color breeding and potentially a major stud/breeder plant. Take those "crappy shape-feedback" naysayers off the recipient list!

I don't necessarily like my options to the question. It's either amazing or it's compost??!? I don't know the answer.
Question is ... why is this more or less worthy than Legacy? Because Legacy was the first white top/red throat clone??
Everyone says they have a 'version'. I would bet money that someone has a better clone than Legacy. But, is it the first to the finish line or is it the best clone with these traits? This whole thing is bullshit. It's getting as bad as orchids did 15 years ago. Who knows if this one should be registered ... YET. It's not mature . It's definitely NOT compost. Well done Mike. Screw the other opinions. No one asked whether Chas Brew should be registered. If someone comes up with a better clone than Legacy can we strip the cultivar status of Legacy? NO. So ... here we are.
That is EXACTLY what I thought when I saw this plant. It is amazing! But it looks very similar to Legacy, which is regarded as an extremely rare clone. Is it because Legacy is larger than the other clones? I don't know because I don't grow Legacy, but I have a number of young seedlings with similar traits to Legacy and the combination of traits seem to happen a good amount in different sizes and shapes. 

As you said, it is a very nice plant but similar to other clones so I would continue to grow it but I wouldn't register.

posts.body_html:
Mike, I like the look of this plant but in all honesty I think the "throw out your best ball first" mentality may have bit you in the ass on this one. It's going to be hard for you to follow up S.'Ellie Wang' with something that is middle of the line when your first cultivar was a top of the line plant. You've set the bar so high with EW that everyone is going to expect perfection from everything you name, or contemplate naming.

Would I grow this plant in my collection? I would say more than likely yes. Is it a must have? No. Would it be worthy of naming after your son? Definitely not. You're son needs something named that fits his personality. Between everything I've read here and the countless emails we've sent I've come to the conclusion that Ellie (your daughter) is a real firecracker, so a plant that reminds you of that is perfect for her and EW does that.

Besides everybody here knows you have better material in there somewhere brother 😉

On a side note. Thanks for the contact on that permit stuff I emailed you about, even though it is sounding like it's going to be a long, tedious process.

Heath
